correctness.rationale: For each target, increasing source positions correspond bijectively to a copy-index sequence constrained at each weak descent; removing the cumulative weak descents yields a stars-and-bars binomial formula. Optimal target lengths are complete q-blocks when m>=2, and equality forces the precise repeated permutation. Explicit consecutive coefficient ratios prove strict log-concavity. A negative-binomial sum proves the rational GF, whose unique simple positive pole supplies the exponential constant, and Stirling with the unique interior saddle proves the negative one-half logarithmic correction. Checks of independent DP enumerations and exact finite generating-function coefficients completed successfully; no infinite proof rests on finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: Direct primary-text comparison with Fang (2024 AofA and expanded 2025, Sections 3–4), Menon–Singh (2023), and Bukh–Saatashvili (2025) distinguishes the new fixed many-letter cyclic-source all-target classification from the previously covered binary alternating case, general rationality for fixed periodic source-target pairs, binary source optimization, and global large-alphabet bounds. No inspected source or searched research record implies the exact q>=3 maximizer classification. The constructed rate bound is a strict improvement over Fang’s particular all-alphabet upper bound but may be superseded by later constructions for large q; that limitation is explicit.
residual_risks: The repeated-permutation weak-descent count may have an equivalent formulation in older generalized binomial coefficients or lattice-path literature not captured by title/semantic search.
Fang’s all-alphabet upper bound is not necessarily the sharpest available for large q because Bukh and Saatashvili provide improved asymptotic information; no such supremacy is claimed.
The originality conclusion rests on inspected accessible publications and searchable records, not an exhaustive proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: For every alphabet size q>=3 this determines the entire, not merely one, set of most frequent subsequences for a canonical balanced periodic source, including all possible ties and its complete bivariate occurrence generating function. The structural rigidity converts a well-motivated combinatorics-on-words extremal problem into an explicit alphabet-dependent asymptotic, improving Fang’s all-alphabet bound at q=3 by about 0.0843 bits per symbol. The result does not pretend to compute the exact global minimum and acknowledges later stronger large-alphabet global estimates.
